summary: Fujio Taniguchi specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Nagoya University in 1991 under Musashi Tachikawa, having also studied under Yusho Miyasaka, Zuiho Yamaguchi, Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar, Kaiun Shiradate, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

Fumihiko Sueki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religion. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura, Kyosho Hayashima, and Yoshiro Tamura, later serving there as professor (1995–2009) and at Nichibunken (around 2009–2015).

Fumimaro Watanabe (1934–1990) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto (PhD under A. K. Warder), he was a professor at Kindai University (1981) and Aichi Gakuin University (1987).

Fumio Enomoto is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He was a research assistant at Kyoto University (around 1981–1984) and later served as a professor at Osaka University from around 1998 to 2017.

Fumio Masutani (1902–1987) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. A University of Tokyo graduate, he served as professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (around 1953–1965) and Taisho University (around 1965–1973), and president of Tsuru University (1969–1971).

Fumio Matsuda is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who held a post at Komazawa University. In 1997, he was attested as executive committee chairman for the Japanese Association for the Study of Indian Religions' 40th conference.

Fumio Ouchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He received his doctorate from Otani University, where he served as associate professor (around 1993–2000) and professor (around 2000–2013).

Fumio Shoji is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Rissho University from around 1998 to 2007 and served as an assistant professor in its Faculty of Buddhist Studies from around 2013 to 2018.
Fumio Tamamuro is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University from around 1954 to 1962 and later held a post there from around 1976 to 2006.

Futoshi Omae is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1991) and held a post at Shimane Prefectural Junior College of International Studies (attested 1997).

Futoshi Takehashi is a Buddhist studies scholar. He pursued doctoral studies at Otani University (attested 1992) and served as an assistant at the Institute of Shin Buddhist Studies from 1995 to 1997.

Fyodor Buslaev (1818–1897) worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of Moscow University from around 1834 to 1838 and joined the faculty of Moscow State University in 1846.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (1866–1942) was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Minaev, Bühler, and Jacobi, he was a Saint Petersburg professor (around 1900–1941) and Imperial Academy of Sciences member (1910).

Félix Nève (1816–1893) was a Belgian scholar of Indology and linguistics. After studying at KU Leuven, Christian Lassen, Friedrich Wilhelm Thiersch, and Eugène Burnouf, he served as a professor at KU Leuven from 1841 until becoming emeritus in 1877.

G. C. Nayak (1935–2021) was an Indian scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held appointments as a fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (around 1989–1991) and senior fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (1996).

G. Thomas Tanselle studied at Yale University (BA around 1951–1955). He taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1960–1978) and Columbia University (around 1978), and served as vice president of the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation (1978–2006).
G. V. Aston works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Aston earned a PhD in philosophy at the University of Canterbury (1986–2004), studying under Jack Copeland and Paul Harrison.

id: P:Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso
summary: Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso studied under Tenzin Gyatso and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gadjin M. Nagao (1907–2005) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University under Susumu Yamaguchi and Ryotai Hatani, subsequently serving as professor and holding the Chair of Buddhist Studies there from 1935 to 1971.

Gail Hinich Sutherland is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Chicago under advisers Wendy Doniger and Carol Bolon, as well as traditional teacher Virendra Singh.
